messages.author: c6ca7877bef91eef
messages.subject: Defining Multiple Outputs
parts:
I have the following code in my server.R, where I am defining outputs result1 and result2. The number of result variables can be different from 2. Currently, I am using a brew template to generate multiple output functions in server.R. My question is whether there exists a more elegant functional programming approach that can generate multiple result outputs. Maybe reactiveList?

output$result1 <- reactive(function(){
  if (input$run1 == 0)
    return()
  return(isolate({
    runCode(input$code1)
  }))
})

output$result2 <- reactive(function(){
  if (input$run2 == 0)
    return()
  return(isolate({
    runCode(input$code2)
  }))
})

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Defining Multiple Outputs
parts:
I would expect this to work (can't say I've actually tried it though):

for (i in 1:10) {
  output[[paste('result', i, sep='')]] <- reactive(function(){
    if (input[[paste('run', i, sep='')]] == 0)
      return()
    return(isolate({
      runCode(input[[paste('code', i, sep='')]])
    }))
  })
}

I'm not sure when we added the [[]] operator for input/output, I think it was sometime between Shiny 0.3.1 and 0.4.0 though. The latter is just hitting CRAN now.
